steps: Classify a reproducible request with the public triage taxonomy.
Use a public issue or governance discussion to leave an auditable handoff when no maintainer is available.
Start from the versioned release rehearsal and record the exact blocked gate.
Leave the tag or rollback decision in a public issue for the maintainer to resume.
Use private vulnerability reporting when enabled, without opening a public issue.
If unavailable, contact the maintainer privately and retain only a redacted reproduction.
Open a public RFC with compatibility, privacy, security, and evidence impact.
Keep the change on hold until a second reviewer is named or the risk is explicitly accepted.
Freeze new adapter capability claims when owner or backup acknowledgement is missing.
Replay the lifecycle evidence and route a deprecation or migration decision through a public issue.
Record a dependency-aware issue with acceptance criteria and evidence references.
Do not mark an item complete until the merged-main reproduction and limitations are retained.

onboarding.entrypoint: Read docs/COMMUNITY_FEEDBACK.md and the issue templates.
onboarding.expected: Classify bugs, features, compatibility reports, contributor signals, and security reports without exposing private data.

onboarding.entrypoint: Request a minimal sanitized reproduction and exact runtime details.
onboarding.expected: A maintainer can replay the report locally or record a bounded failure without treating an issue as a support guarantee.
The operator can identify the package/tag, compatibility, artifact, provenance, and rollback gates before creating a tag.

onboarding.entrypoint: Run the offline release and compatibility validators from a clean source state.
onboarding.expected: A failed gate is recorded as a no-go with the exact command and no release mutation is attempted.
A reporter knows the private intake route, safe reproduction boundary, and prohibited public disclosure paths.

onboarding.entrypoint: Use a synthetic redacted report and the adapter lifecycle response steps.
onboarding.expected: The report can be contained and replayed without collecting credentials, source bodies, network data, or public exploit details.

onboarding.entrypoint: Read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/CHANGE_CONTROL.md, and the public RFC process.
onboarding.expected: A contributor can distinguish a routine fix from a material contract change that needs an RFC and compatibility evidence.

onboarding.entrypoint: Run the focused test and full local check commands before proposing a merge.
onboarding.expected: The change retains deterministic fixtures, negative coverage, privacy checks, and the exact local toolchain record.
A proposed adapter names its construct slice, owner, backup, compatibility dimensions, evidence, and explicit non-goals.

onboarding.entrypoint: Replay conformance, isolation, packaging, and lifecycle validators for a synthetic adapter.
onboarding.expected: Owner gaps freeze promotion and releases instead of silently widening the support claim.
A coordinator can find prerequisites, acceptance criteria, issue identity, and the evidence gate for a proposed task.

onboarding.entrypoint: Use CONTRIBUTING.md completion evidence and rerun the merged-main reproduction.
onboarding.expected: A roadmap item remains open when hosted or platform evidence is unavailable; no unsupported completion claim is made.

dryRuns.scenario: Synthetic contributor follows the public setup, formatting, lint, typecheck, and focused resilience-test path without editing or pushing source.
friction: The path is documented, but a second human reviewer is not currently staffed.
The supported Node window is 22.x and 24.x; this local rehearsal used compatible Node 26.7.0 and does not expand that support claim.

dryRuns.scenario: Synthetic release-triager follows the no-write compatibility, Action-fixture, documentation-link, and roadmap validation path without creating a tag, issue, or release.
friction: The dry run can prove command reachability and no-write behavior, but cannot prove that a second human will acknowledge a future incident.
Hosted checks and GitHub mutations are intentionally outside this offline rehearsal.

risks.finding: Only @AlisinaDevelo is a current named maintainer; the public triage route is documented but no staffed backup is observed.
risks.mitigation: Keep the taxonomy, issue templates, and handoff steps public; record a second maintainer only after sustained reviewed stewardship.

risks.finding: Release and rollback authority remains with the current maintainer; the rehearsal is a route, not release permission.
risks.mitigation: Require the versioned release rehearsal and public no-go record before a second release owner is staffed.

risks.finding: Private vulnerability intake has a documented fallback, but no independent security responder is observed.
risks.mitigation: Use private intake, synthetic or redacted reproductions, and the adapter containment sequence; do not publish exploit details while ownership is unresolved.

risks.finding: Graph, evidence, and CLI compatibility decisions have one current named owner and no verified backup reviewer.
risks.mitigation: Require an RFC, focused tests, compatibility evidence, and explicit second-reviewer assignment before material contract changes merge.

risks.finding: Adapter policies name role-based backups, but current staffing of those roles is not observed in the public snapshot.
risks.mitigation: Freeze promotion on owner gaps, replay lifecycle fixtures, and require a named owner and backup before graduation.

risks.finding: Roadmap sequencing, issue reconciliation, and evidence closure remain maintainer-led; a public manifest is not a staffed operations team.
risks.mitigation: Keep dependencies and acceptance criteria machine-readable and leave every closure linked to merged-main evidence.

risks.finding: A role map reduces discovery cost, but the repository has no independent human rehearsal record or staffed handoff acknowledgement.
risks.mitigation: Repeat the two role rehearsals with an actual non-author contributor when available and publish friction without collecting private telemetry.

provenance.source: CARTOGRAPH repository-authored maintainer resilience rehearsal fixture
provenance.reference: M-008 contributor and maintainer single-point-of-failure issue; no external participant record
provenance.transformation: The report encodes public ownership and onboarding paths plus two synthetic non-author role rehearsals; it retains no contributor identity, source body, private report, hosted check, network trace, or telemetry.
